THE BUG, measured on a real episode. video_stem_recipe() in server/pipeline/av_sync.py hard-codes every speaker stem to 960x540:
    "setpts=PTS-STARTPTS,fps=30,scale=960:540:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=960:540:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2:black,setsar=1"
The real source cameras for this episode are 1920x1080 (host) and 1280x720 (guest). Everything downstream (composite, angle-switched program, final render) is 1920x1080, so the pipeline DESTROYS resolution and then upscales it back: the finished 1080p master measures ~30% less high-frequency detail than the raw camera (detail score 2.1 vs 3.0 on the same subject). The owner's requirement is explicit: always keep the HD source quality.

THE FIX: make the stem canvas a named constant STEM_CANVAS_W x STEM_CANVAS_H = 1920x1080 (the delivery format), replacing the 960x540 literals in the normalize filter, and expose it as an optional parameter of video_stem_recipe (canvas=(w,h), default the constants) so a caller can override. Keep force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease + pad + setsar=1 exactly as now, so a 1280x720 source is letterboxed onto the 1920x1080 canvas without distortion and a 1920x1080 source maps 1:1 with no rescale. Keep fps=30 and the two-step (hole-fill then place) structure UNCHANGED. Do not touch audio stems, timing, tpad placement, or the content pin logic — only the pixel canvas.

Encoding: the stems are now 4x the pixels, so also make the encode quality explicit rather than accidental — keep the existing _h264_encode_args() call path unchanged (do not lower crf), but add a short comment noting that 1080p stems are ~4x larger on disk by design and that the previous 540p canvas was silent quality loss.

TESTS (tests/test_stem_resolution.py, pure string/arg assertions on the returned commands, no ffmpeg execution; at least 4): (1) the normalize filter targets 1920:1080 in BOTH the scale and pad stages; (2) NEGATIVE: no returned command contains "960:540" or "960x540" anywhere; (3) a custom canvas kwarg is honored in both scale and pad; (4) force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease and setsar=1 are still present (no-distortion guard); (5) the step-B placement command still carries tpad with the given grid offset and the session length -t. Keep existing tests green; if an existing test asserts 960:540, UPDATE it with a one-line comment citing the measured detail loss.

OWNED FILES (only these):
  server/pipeline/promo_clips.py
  tests/test_promo_clips.py
  tests/test_speaker_framing.py

THE BUG, proven by frame inspection on a real published-quality clip. Vertical (9:16) promo clips are framed with speaker_half_crop() in server/pipeline/promo_clips.py, which crops the LEFT half for a host segment and the RIGHT half for a guest segment. That logic assumes the source frame is a SIDE-BY-SIDE two-camera layout. It is not: the source is the FINAL edited program, which is ANGLE-SWITCHED — a single speaker fills the entire 1920x1080 frame at any moment. Cropping the "guest half" of a full-frame shot of the guest therefore returns the WALL BEHIND HIM. The shipped clip literally shows a blurry wall with picture frames and no face, while the same timestamp in the final shows the guest centered in frame. The owner's words: "it isn't on his face, it's on the side and off center."

THE FIX — frame the crop on the actual speaker:
1. Add detect_face_center_x(video_path, start_s, duration_s, *, samples=FACE_SAMPLE_COUNT) that samples FACE_SAMPLE_COUNT (named constant, 9) evenly spaced frames across the clip span via ffmpeg (decode single frames to a temp PNG or raw gray buffer), runs OpenCV's haarcascade_frontalface_default (cv2.data.haarcascades) on each, and returns the MEDIAN horizontal center of the largest face per sampled frame, plus a confidence = fraction of samples where a face was found. Import cv2 lazily inside the function so the module still imports where OpenCV is absent, and return (None, 0.0) on ImportError or when no face is found in any sample.
2. Add speaker_framed_crop(src_w, src_h, center_x=None) returning an ffmpeg crop expression for a 9:16 window: crop_w = round(src_h * 9 / 16) (clamped to src_w), x = center_x - crop_w/2 CLAMPED to [0, src_w - crop_w], full height, x rounded to an even integer (encoder-safe). center_x=None means centered on the frame.
3. Change the vertical-clip path to: detect the face over the clip span; if confidence >= FACE_CONFIDENCE_MIN (named constant, 0.34, i.e. a face in at least a third of samples) use speaker_framed_crop centered on the detected face; otherwise fall back to a CENTER 9:16 crop and log the fallback reason. The half-crop must no longer be used for full-frame sources.
4. KEEP speaker_half_crop for genuine side-by-side sources, but gate it: only use it when the caller explicitly declares the source layout as side-by-side (e.g. a layout="side_by_side" argument or an explicit is_side_by_side flag). Default layout for the final program is "full_frame". Never silently half-crop a full-frame source.

TESTS (tests/test_speaker_framing.py, pure math/string assertions plus a synthetic OpenCV-free path; at least 5): (1) speaker_framed_crop centered on a face at x=1400 in a 1920x1080 frame yields crop width 608 and an x that keeps the window fully inside the frame; (2) a face near the left edge (x=50) clamps x to 0, never negative; (3) a face near the right edge clamps to src_w - crop_w; (4) center_x=None yields the exact center window; (5) NEGATIVE: the vertical path with layout="full_frame" produces a filter chain containing NO half-width crop (assert the crop width is the 9:16 window, not src_w//2); (6) detect_face_center_x returns (None, 0.0) and the caller falls back to center crop when cv2 is unavailable (monkeypatch the import to raise ImportError) — the pipeline must degrade, never crash; (7) x offsets are even integers. Mock all ffmpeg subprocess calls; do not decode real video in tests.

THE PROBLEM. Episode.create() in server/models/episode.py builds its directory name from the TOPIC, not the guest:
    slug = topic or "guest"
    slug = slug.lower().replace(" ", "-")[:30]
    dir_name = f"{date_str}-{slug}"
The real episodes/ directory is therefore inconsistent and unbrowsable by person — actual folders include "2026-03-09-5-mistakes-i-made-opening-my-s", "2026-03-18-leadership-mindset-&-building-", "2026-07-17-what-100-conversations-with-op" (truncated titles, one with a raw "&"), alongside correct person folders like "2026-06-10-fred-cho". The owner wants every episode folder identified by the GUEST.

THE FIX: derive the slug from the guest identity first, topic only as fallback.
1. Add a module-level slugify(value) helper: lowercase; replace any run of non-alphanumeric characters with a single hyphen; strip leading/trailing hyphens; collapse repeats; truncate to a named MAX_SLUG_LEN (40) WITHOUT leaving a trailing hyphen or splitting mid-word where avoidable (truncate at the last hyphen before the limit when one exists past half the limit).
2. Slug precedence: (a) explicit guest_name argument if Episode.create accepts/receives one — inspect the real signature and use what exists, including any guest name available on the guests list entries; (b) a name parsable from the first guest LinkedIn URL slug (e.g. .../in/fred-cho-12345 -> "fred-cho", stripping trailing numeric id segments); (c) the topic, slugified; (d) the literal "guest". Document the order in the docstring.
3. Keep the date prefix format exactly as now: f"{date_str}-{slug}". Do not rename existing directories and do not add migration logic — this governs NEW episodes only. If a directory of that name already exists, disambiguate deterministically with a -2, -3 suffix rather than colliding.

TESTS (tests/test_episode_slug.py, pure, tmp_path for any filesystem use; at least 4): (1) a guest name "Fred Cho" yields "<date>-fred-cho" even when a long topic is supplied (guest wins); (2) a LinkedIn URL like https://www.linkedin.com/in/fred-cho-8814/ with no explicit name yields "fred-cho" with the numeric id stripped; (3) NEGATIVE: a topic like "Leadership Mindset & Building!" used as fallback never produces "&", never a trailing hyphen, and never exceeds MAX_SLUG_LEN (assert against the real observed bad names); (4) with neither guest nor topic the slug is "guest"; (5) a colliding directory produces a -2 suffix rather than reusing the existing directory.
